mcp.title: Agent access (MCP)
mcp.description: A loopback control service an MCP bridge may call, so an agent can look at your sessions and, if you allow it, change them. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, and every call presents a token that this window never sees.

switch.label: Allow agent access
switch.help: Off unless you turn it on. While it is on, this machine opens one port on the loopback interface and writes the token a bridge needs to a file only your account can read. Turning it off closes the port and deletes that file.

status.heading: Listener
status.countNote: The count and the port come from the listener, not from the settings file — what is written down and what is running are two answers.

config.title: Client configuration
config.description: The snippet below is copied, not shown: put it in your MCP client's configuration file. It names the bridge and the endpoint file, and it carries no token — the bridge reads the secret from that file itself.

fields.heading: Settings
fields.portHint: Zero lets the system choose a free port, which is what a fresh install does. The bridge learns the number from the endpoint file, so a fixed port is only needed if something else expects one.
fields.approvalTimeoutHint: How long a call waits for your answer before it is refused. A question nobody answers must not hold an agent's connection open for ever.
fields.retentionDaysHint: How many days the audit file is kept. Each call is one line; nothing is pruned before this.
fields.maxResultHint: The most one call may return, so a huge directory listing or a long log cannot push everything else out of an agent's context. Longer results are truncated and marked.
fields.saved: Saved. The listener will start with these settings.
fields.savedRestarted: Saved. The listener restarted with these settings.
fields.restartRequired: Saved, but the listener did not restart — turn it off and on again to apply them.

scope.readOnlyHint: Listing and reading: sessions, directory listings, text files, containers and cluster objects. Nothing runs and nothing is written.
scope.safeWriteHint: Also runs commands and writes remote text files. A destructive command still stops and asks you first.
scope.highRiskHint: Everything the tools offer, including container and cluster changes that are usually destructive — and those still stop and ask you first.

audit.title: Recent activity
audit.description: The tail of this machine's audit file: who called what, how it ended, and how long it took. Nothing here holds a credential or the text a call read.
audit.empty: No agent has called this build yet.

approval.title: An agent is asking to act
approval.description: Nothing has been sent yet. This call is held until you answer, and it is refused if the question is ignored.
approval.subject: What it would do

hostKey.title: This host's key is not one this device has seen
hostKey.body: Approving lets this one call connect. The fingerprint is what the host presented; check it against the machine yourself if you do not know it.

approval.failed: The answer could not be delivered. The request is still waiting.
